system_prompt:
You are taking the TIMSS mathematics test for students in the eighth grade. Answer each question as well as you can.

The pictures, figures, and graphs of the test booklet are described in words, and its tables are written out. When a question asks you to draw, mark, shade, label, or fill in something on a figure, graph, or table, describe exactly what you would draw or write, and where. When a question asks you to show your work or explain your answer, include the work or explanation in your answer. For a multiple-choice question, choose one option.
user_prompt:
Ryan is packing books into a rectangular box.

All the books are the same size.

[Image: A book and a box. The book measures 20 centimeters by 15 centimeters by 6 centimeters. The box has a length of 36 centimeters, width of 30 centimeters, and height of 20 centimeters.]

What is the largest number of books that will fit inside the box?

Answer: ____

Figure, described in words:
Two 3-dimensional diagrams:
1. A closed rectangular book labeled "Book" with dimensions indicated by double-headed arrows: height/thickness 6 cm, length 20 cm along the left edge, and width 15 cm along the right-front edge.
2. An open rectangular box labeled "Box" with dimensions indicated by double-headed arrows: width 30 cm along the front-left top edge, length 36 cm along the back-right top edge, and vertical height/depth of 20 cm along the inside back corner from top to bottom.

answer.description: Your answer to the question, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer.title: Answer

output.answer: Box volume = 36 x 30 x 20 = 21600 cubic cm. Book volume = 20 x 15 x 6 = 1800 cubic cm. Check orientations: the box dimensions 36, 30, 20 can each be matched by book dimensions 20, 15, 6. Try 36 = 6 x 6 (6 books along length), 30 = 15 x 2 (2 books along width), 20 = 20 x 1 (1 book along height): 6 x 2 x 1 = 12 books. Other arrangement: 36 = 20 ... not divisible; 36 = 6x6, 30 = 15x2, 20 = 20x1 gives 12. Try 36 = 6x6, 30 = 6x5 no (book dims are 20,15,6: 30 = 15x2 or 6x5 with the 20-side unused, 20 = 20 along height): 36 = 6 x 6 (6 books), 30 = 6 x 5 (5 books), 20 = ... remaining 20 needs book side 20 but used 6 and 6 already... Orientation with book's 6 along length (6 books), 6 along width (5 books), 20 along height (1 book) gives 6 x 5 x 1 = 30 books. Check: 6 x 5 x 1 = 30, and 30 x 1800 = 54000 which exceeds the box volume 21600, so this is impossible; recheck: book dimension 6 along 36 gives 6 books; book dimension 6 along 30 gives 5 books; book dimension 20 along 20 gives 1 book, and the book's remaining 15 must lie in the 20 direction... the book footprint is 15 x 6 in the 36x30 plane, so the arrangement must use book sides 6 (height/thickness) and 15 or 20 in the plane. Best packing: book with thickness 6 along the 20 cm height is impossible (height 20 can take 20 or 15 or 6 but only 3 layers of 6 with leftover 2). Considering book sides 20 x 15 along 36 x 30 face and 6 along 20 height: 36 = 20 + ... 20x15 footprint: 30 = 15 x 2 gives 2 books with 20 along 36 leaves 16 unused; 36 = 20 leaves 16 unused, so 1 book per layer of 20x15 footprint... better: footprint 15 x 6 with 15 along 30 (2 books) and 6 along 36 (6 books) = 12 per layer, height 20 with thickness 20 stacking 1 layer: 12 books. Alternatively thickness 6 vertical: footprint 20 x 15 in 36 x 30: 20 along 36 (1), 15 along 30 (2) = 2 per layer, 20/6 = 3 layers: 6 books. Footprint 15 x 20 with 20 along 30 (1) and 15 along 36 (2): 2 per layer, 3 layers = 6. Best is 12. Largest number of books that will fit: 12.
